title: [switchorch] No vendor-neutral way to disable the VOQ credit watchdog via SWITCH_TABLE
author: darius-nexthop
body:
**Is it platform specific**

Affects VOQ switches which implement support for the SAI attribute.

**Importance or Severity**

Medium

**Description**

SwitchOrch exposes a range of `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_*` knobs through APPL_DB SWITCH_TABLE, but there is no field for the VOQ hardware credit watchdog (`SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD` / `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD_TIMER`).

On VOQ platforms the credit watchdog ages out and drains queues that stop receiving scheduler credits. That is exactly the condition some tests and tooling create on purpose. For example, [snappi](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/tree/master/tests/snappi_tests) ECN-marking tests build up a lossless egress queue with a PFC pause storm, the watchdog trips, and the queued packets are dropped.

Today, the only ways to disable it are vendor-specific:

1. A raw bcmcmd register poke (not portable, not always available on newer Broadcom platforms)
2. The sai_thrift path (drags in a syncd-RPC image dependency for a single knob).

**Current Behavior**

SwitchOrch's SWITCH_TABLE attribute map has no entry for the credit watchdog, so `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD` / `_TIMER` cannot be reached from configuration. Disabling the watchdog requires vendor-specific `bcmcmd` or `sai_thrift`.

**Proposed Behavior**

SWITCH_TABLE should expose `credit_watchdog` / `credit_watchdog_timer` fields mapping to `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD` / `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD_TIMER`, gated on `SAI_SWITCH_TYPE_VOQ` (skipped with a log notice on non-VOQ switches), giving any VOQ platform a vendor-neutral way to control the credit watchdog over the standard APPL_DB path.

Requires SAI headers with `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD` / `_TIMER` (added in opencomputeproject/SAI#1779, released in SAI v1.12.0).

linkedPullRequests.title: switchorch: add credit_watchdog SWITCH_TABLE knob
linkedPullRequests.author: darius-nexthop
linkedPullRequests.body:
**What I did**

Added `credit_watchdog` and `credit_watchdog_timer` to the SwitchOrch `SWITCH_TABLE` attribute map. These map to the SAI attributes `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD` and `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD_TIMER` respectively.

This allows the VOQ credit watchdog for supported platforms to be controlled through the standard SAI switch-attribute path driven via APPL_DB.

Both attributes are gated by `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_TYPE == SAI_SWITCH_TYPE_VOQ` so setting them on non-VOQ switches will be skipped with a log notice. We also define `gMySwitchType` in p4orch test main to fix linker errors.

**Why I did it**

There is currently no vendor-neutral way to disable the VOQ hardware credit watchdog. Today, [for example in Snappi](https://github.com/nexthop-ai/sonic-mgmt/blob/master/tests/common/snappi_tests/common_helpers.py#L833-L860), the only method is via a bcmcmd, which is not supported on latest BCM platforms.

The alternatives are using platform shell commands to write explicit registers, exposing vendor-specific implementation details, or `sai_thrift`, introducing a dependency on the syncd RPC swap image which snappi tests today have no reason to rely on.

Exposing the attribute via `SWITCH_TABLE` makes the knob available to tests and tooling on any VOQ platform.

**How I verified it**

- New DVS test `test_switch.py::TestSwitch::test_credit_watchdog_non_voq` verifies the fields are skipped on a non-VOQ switch without blocking other attributes in the same batch.
- New DVS test `test_virtual_chassis.py::TestVirtualChassis::test_voq_switch_credit_watchdog` verifies the attributes are programmed on a VOQ switch.
- Verified on Broadcom DNX VOQ hardware: writing `credit_watchdog=0` via `SWITCH_TABLE` (using `swssconfig`) disables the credit watchdog and writing `1` restores it.

**Details if related**

Requires SAI headers with `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD` / `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD_TIMER` (added in [opencomputeproject/SAI#1779](https://github.com/opencomputeproject/SAI/pull/1779), first released in SAI v1.12.0).

Changes validated on SAI 14.1.

Related to sonic-net/sonic-mgmt#25152

Fixes #4705

comments.author: darius-nexthop
comments.body:
> @darius-nexthop Can you please share how are we enabling/disabling credit-wd during runtime ? Are tests going to explicitly call set to configure or is there another way ? Also, if user like to turn on by default for all snappi tests. is there way ?

Hi @vmittal-msft, yes it would be an explicit set. 

The plan is to keep Snappi changes minimal by only updating the existing [`disable_packet_aging()` / `enable_packet_aging()` helpers](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/3ae22ef8deb0b37464ff691f7f8edb0fc4be8844/tests/common/snappi_tests/common_helpers.py#L833-L890), which today use "BCMSAI credit-watchdog disable".

Instead, the helper just needs to write the field into APPL_DB's SWITCH_TABLE at runtime, which SwitchOrch translates to the SAI attribute (the logic in this PR):

```py
db = DBConnector("APPL_DB", 0, True)
p = ProducerStateTable(db, "SWITCH_TABLE")
p.set("switch", [("credit_watchdog", "0")])   # "0" = off, "1" = on
```

I validated this end-to-end on a DNX VOQ linecard. The APPL_DB write flips `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD` in ASIC_DB and the HW credit-watchdog register, works for both directions.

If we want this applied by default across snappi tests, we just issue the APPL_DB write once in a session-scoped fixture rather than per-test. @atul-nexthop may be able to share more regarding test plans.

comments.author: atul-nexthop
darius-nexthop
comments.body:
~~Snappi tests utilize GCU to apply patches. GCU performs YANG validation. We are working on adding YANG validation for the new credit-watchdog attribute, do not merge this PR until complete. Thanks!~~

Disregard the above, this doesn't require a YANG change.

This change adds an APPL_DB field. YANG validation applies to CONFIG_DB, so APPL_DB switch attributes do not require (and have never had) YANG models. This is consistent with every existing field in the same SWITCH_TABLE attribute map, none of which are YANG-modeled (e.g., `fdb_aging_time`).

Consumers should therefore write this knob into APPL_DB, which drives `SAI_SWITCH_ATTR_CREDIT_WD` through SwitchOrch.

YANG validation *would* become relevant if a future use case needs this in `config_db.json`. However, that would also require a new model of the full SWITCH table in YANG, which is out of scope here and independent of this orchagent change.
